canonical_data: A local data database holding sessions and runtime state, plus workspace files and a Markdown memory tree with embeddings kept on the user's disk
current_repo_note: Covers the open-source desktop app and runtime in this repository. The built-in default model account, the HolaHub recipe platform, and the enterprise tier with SSO and audit logs the README describes are vendor-operated and not reviewed here, and the integration connectors run through a third-party broker. The same shared memory could support a memory reading, but the documented outcome is delegated work across apps, so it is recorded as a work agent. Claude Code and Codex remain separately licensed host agents.
strengths: Hosts three agents, Claude Code, Codex, and its own, over one runtime that shares memory, tools, skills, and apps, so a person can switch agents without rebuilding the setup
Memory is stored locally as plain files a person can read, edit, and delete, backed by a local state store, with embeddings for recall
A large TypeScript runtime with a unit-test tree beside each service, covering the API server, channel gateway, harness host, and cron worker
weaknesses: The licence is Apache 2.0 with added conditions that forbid offering it as a hosted service or embedding it in a product sold to third parties and protect the interface branding, so it is source-available rather than open source

The licence defines the protected frontend as a desktop directory that does not exist at that path in the tree, where the app lives under apps/desktop, leaving the scope of the branding condition ambiguous

The repository was created in March 2026, and the zero-setup path routes inference through the vendor's own account, with integrations run through a third-party broker, so the local-first claim depends on the bring-your-own-keys route
why_it_matters: A heavily starred attempt to make the agent a workspace rather than a chat, hosting the incumbent coding agents alongside embedded apps and one user-owned memory.
